# Agent guide

A 3D model of Huế in the browser (three.js, Vite, no backend). This page lists what a capable newcomer could get wrong
on a first visit. Details live in [docs/development.md](docs/development.md); history and work in progress in
[PROGRESS.md](PROGRESS.md).

## Source and generated files

| Edit this | Not this |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/build-data.mjs`, `scripts/frame.json`, `data/` (OSM extracts, terrain, heights, `control-points.json`) | `public/data/hue.json` and `public/data/places.json`: generated by `npm run data:build`; hand edits are lost on the next build |
| `src/` (scene, landmarks, UI), `public/data/stories.json` (card stories, written by hand) | `dist/`: generated by `npm run build` |

After changing anything under `scripts/` or `data/`, run `npm run data:build` and commit the regenerated
`public/data/*.json` with the change. Fix a problem where it starts (source data, parser, shared builder), not in one place downstream.

## Coordinates

Scene units are metres: **x east, y up, z south**, origin at the middle of cầu Trường Tiền. The river surface is
y 0 and the city's ground is y 2.6 (`LAND_Y` in `src/config.js`); hills rise above that (`groundY` in
`src/geo/terrain.js`).

`places` in `hue.json` store x and z in **decimetres**. Ngọ Môn is stored `x: -10345, z: 1315`, so in the scene it
stands at x −1034.5, z 131.5: about 1 km west and 130 m south of the bridge. Kỳ Đài (`z: 2860`) is further south,
in front of the gate, as it is in Huế. `buildPlaces` hands a place file its record already in metres; everything
reading `data.places` directly must divide by 10.

## Adding or changing a landmark

- One place, one file: `src/landmarks/places/<slug>.js` exporting `id` (the place's id in `hue.json`) and
  `build({ data, S, group, place, THREE })`. The contract is at the top of `src/landmarks/places/index.js`. Vite picks
  the file up in the browser and `scripts/lib/scene.mjs` picks it up for the geometry checks; nothing to register.
- A builder outside `places/` goes into `buildLandmarks` in `src/landmarks/build.js`, the one sequence both the
  browser (`src/main.js`) and the geometry checks (`scripts/lib/scene.mjs`) run. Don't call builders from
  `main.js` directly, or the checks will not see them.
- Documented heights go in `docs/heights-reference.json` with their source and confidence; `check:heights` holds the
  model to them.
- Research notes per place go in `docs/places/`.

## Verify before asking for review

```bash
npm ci
npm run check                                   # version, data, heights, burial, overlap, joints, roofs (CI)
npm run build                                   # production build (CI runs this)
node scripts/shot.mjs --view ngo-mon-arrival    # a named view → scratch/shots/ngo-mon-arrival/
node scripts/shot.mjs ngomon                    # one place from four sides and above
node scripts/compare.mjs ngo-mon-arrival        # before/after vs origin/main → scratch/compare/index.html
```

- Named views live in `scripts/views.json`: a fixed camera, or an arrival (start pose, the visitor's pick of a place,
  frames at set seconds). They run with `?still`, so repeat runs of a view match to within a few
  scattered pixels (GPU noise; a real change shows as a region). Add a view when
  a task needs one; don't move an existing one, or older captures stop being comparable.
- Shots need Google Chrome (`CHROME=` to point elsewhere); they use the GPU by default, `SHOT_GL=swiftshader` for
  software rendering (slow).
- `window.__hue` exposes the scene in the browser; `__hue.step(dt)` advances one frame.
- `scratch/` is ignored by git; put captures and throwaway output there.

## Pull requests

- Work on a branch; `main` is protected and PRs are squash-merged. Keep one task per branch and worktree.
- Match the evidence to the change: landmark or terrain → checks, build, matched near and far views; camera, search
  or cards → a reproducible visitor journey and frames of the motion; data pipeline → what changed in the generated
  city; performance → measurements on the same scene, viewport and machine.
- Put the before/after frames (from `compare.mjs`) and one sentence on the creative choice in the PR description.

## Ask the owner before

- choosing between sources that disagree about how a building looked, or reconstructing without a source;
- changing what the visitor experiences in a way the issue did not ask for (navigation, defaults, the opening view);
- adding a runtime dependency or a network request (the site loads nothing beyond its own bundle).

Everything else (how to build it, which file, which technique) is yours to decide.
